newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Zedillo to promote development on Guatemala visit.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo to promote development on Guatemala visit.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo will visit Guatemala on Monday to promote development and trade in remote areas on both sides of the Mexican-Guatemalan border, the Mexican embassy said on Sunday.

"The principal object of President Zedillo's work visit is the signing of a sustainable development programme in frontier towns," said Francisco Hernandez, spokesman for the Mexican embassy in Guatemala.

The programme will affect 1.5 million people in 39 towns and cities on both sides of the border, promoting economic and cultural exchange, establishing immigration mechanisms and improving roads and bridges, Hernandez said.

The frontier between Mexico and Guatemala has been a troubled region for decades. During the past 36 years of civil war in Guatemala, leftist rebels operated in the mountains and jungles on the border. In the 1980s tens of thousands of Guatemalan refugees fled to refugee camps in Mexico, escaping violent army attacks on remote Indian villages.
